<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par73 />used to be treated as having a double set of forms, a regular series, and others like {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} without the preformative, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בִּין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=10|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=בִּינֹ֫תִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=9|verse=2}}, also {{GHGheb|text=בַּ֫נְתָּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=רִיב֫וֹתָ|translate=thou strivest}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=13}}, also {{GHGheb|text=רַ֫בְתָּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=3|verse=58}}. The above ''perfects'' ({{GHGheb|text=בִּין}}, {{GHGheb|text=רִיב}}, &c.) might no doubt be taken as forms ''middle ē'' (properly ''ĭ''), the ''ĭ'' of which has been lengthened to ''î'' (like the ''ŭ'' lengthened to ''û'' in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} of {{GHGheb|text=קוּם}}). It is more probable, however, that they are really shortened forms of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}. This is supported by the fact that, especially in the case of {{GHGheb|text=בִּין}}, the shortened forms are few and probably all late, while the corresponding unshortened forms with the same meaning are very numerous, e.g. {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵבִין}} (but {{GHGheb|text=בִּין}} only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=10|verse=1}}), {{GHGheb|text=הֲבִֽינוֹתֶם}}, {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=הָבִין}} (but ''infin. abs.'' {{GHGheb|text=בִּין}} only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=23|verse=1}}), {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=הָבֵן}} (only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=9|verse=23}} {{GHGheb|text=וּבִין}} immediately before {{GHGheb|text=וְהָבֵן}}, also {{GHGheb|text=בִּ֫ינוּ}} three times, and {{GHGheb|text=בִּ֫ינָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=2}}), {{GHGterm|participle}} {{GHGheb|text=מֵבִין}}.<ref>Since {{GHGheb|text=בנת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=2}} might be intended for {{GHGheb|text=בִּנֹ֫תָ}}, there remains really no form of {{GHGheb|text=בין}} which must ''necessarily'' be explained as a Qal, except the ''ptcp. plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=בָּנִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=7}}. Nevertheless it is highly probable that all the above instances of Hiphʿîl-forms, parallel with Qal-forms of the same meaning, are merely due to a secondary formation from the ''imperfects Qal'' {{GHGheb|text=יָבִין}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָשִׂים}}, &c., which were wrongly regarded as ''imperfects Hiphʿîl'': so Barth, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xliii. p. 190 f., and {{GHGcite|title=Nominalbildung}}, p. 119 f.</ref> Elsewhere {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}-forms are in use along with actual {{GHGterm|Qal}}-forms with the same meaning, thus: {{GHGheb|text=מֵרִיב}} (also {{GHGheb|text=רָב}}), {{GHGheb|text=מֵשִׂים|translate=placing}} (but only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=20}}, which, with the critically untenable {{GHGheb|text=הָשִׂ֫ימִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=21}}, is the only instance of {{GHGheb|text=שׂוּם}} in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}), {{GHGheb|text=מֵגִיחַ|translate=breaking forth}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=33}}, with ''infin. Qal'' {{GHGheb|text=גִּיתוֹ}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַחִ֫ישׁוּ|translate=they rushed forth}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=37}}, with {{GHGheb|text=תָשׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=חַ֫שְׁתִּי}}; {{GHGheb|text=מֵצִיץ|translate=glancing}}, also in {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=צָץ}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֵקִיא|translate=he spat out}}, with ''imperat. Qal'' {{GHGheb|text=קְיוּ}}. As ''passives'' we find a few apparent ''imperfects Hophʿal'', which are really (according to {{GHGpar|53|u}}) ''imperfects passive'' of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יוּחַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=66|verse=8}} from {{GHGheb|text=חִיל|translate=to turn round}}, {{GHGheb|text=יוּשָׁר}} from {{GHGheb|text=שִׁיר|translate=to sing}}, {{GHGheb|text=יוּשַׁת}} from {{GHGheb|text=שִׁית|translate=to set}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|73|b}}
'''2.''' The above-mentioned {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}-forms might equally well be derived from verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}; and the influence of the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} is distinctly seen in the {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נָבוֹן}} (ground-form ''nabān''), ''Pôlēl'' {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹנֵן}}, and ''Hithpôlēl'' {{GHGheb|text=הִתְבּוֹנֵן}}. The very close relation existing between verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}} and {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} is evident also from the fact that from some stems both forms occur side by side in {{GHGterm|Qal}}, thus from {{GHGheb|text=חִיל|translate=to turn round, imperative}} also {{GHGheb|text=ח֫וּלִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=4|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=שִׂים|translate=to place, infinitive construct}} commonly {{GHGheb|text=שׂוּם}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=שׂים}} ''Q<sup>e</sup>re''), {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יָשִׂים}}, but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=יָשׂוּם}}. In other verbs one form is, at any rate, the more common, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גִּיל|translate=to exult}} ({{GHGheb|text=גּוּל}} only {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=23|verse=24}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}); from {{GHGheb|text=לוּן}} (perhaps denominative from {{GHGheb|text=לַ֫יִל}}) ''to spend the night'', {{GHGheb|text=לָלוּן}} occurs six times as {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָלִין}} only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=23}}; but the {{GHGterm|imperative}} is always {{GHGheb|text=לִין}}, &c.—Of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״י}} the most common are {{GHGheb|text=שִׁית|translate=to set}}, {{GHGheb|text=רִיב|translate=to strive}}, {{GHGheb|text=דִּין|translate=to judge}}, {{GHGheb|text=שִׂישׂ|translate=to rejoice}}; cf. also {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=בָּל}} (''middle''<section end=par73 /><noinclude>
